A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. The complete texts and appendices are readable, and the original tables, figure images and prompts can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendices A–B report original relevance-assessment, ranking and position-bias experiments using three LLMs and three datasets.

after.justification: The original empirical results remain, supplemented by input-token counts and runtime results in Section 5.1 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The batching strategies, passage permutations, mean score aggregation and Kemeny list aggregation are unchanged. The prompt images are identical; the new discussion of ensemble diversity does not introduce a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate relevance assessment and ranking on TREC DL-19, TREC Covid and Legal Search, using shallow and deep retrieval. The runtime additions reuse this coverage. Naming Thomson Reuters as the Legal Search source does not establish a dataset change.

E2.justification: The original comparisons retain initial retrieval, one-by-one PW and initial-order/shuffled LW baselines. The runtime plots reuse existing method families. Newly cited rankers are not added to the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: V2 adds a distinct runtime evaluation with seconds as an outcome and explicit parallelism controls: one available LLM with m=1, three parallel LLMs with m=1, and three with m=3. This substantially extends evaluation beyond quality and call counts; the original accuracy settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 4 and Appendix C add systematic analysis of how batching, self-consistency and available parallelism affect latency across datasets and retrieval depths. Existing position-bias analyses remain. V2 also removes the qualitative inspection of repeated positional outputs from shuffled LW ranking in Section 5.4.

E5.justification: The new runtime plots report medians with interquartile-range error bars. Existing standard-deviation bands in the position-bias figures are retained unchanged. No additional independent-run counts, seeds or significance tests are disclosed.

E6.justification: V1 Tables 1–3 match v2 Tables 2–4 numerically, and all original plotted results remain identical. V2 adds substantial runtime and token-use results, including reported shallow Legal Search runtimes of 34–58 seconds for sequential one-by-one scoring versus 2–6 seconds for all-in-one scoring, summarized as 6–17x speedups.

T1.justification: The scoring definitions, mean aggregation, Kendall-Tau aggregation description and relevance-probability conversion are unchanged. The expanded ensemble and autoregressive-diversity discussion introduces no formal derivation, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion elevate order-of-magnitude latency reduction to a central contribution, including a 15.3x legal-search example. V1 emphasized quality gains and reduced call counts. The principal accuracy and self-consistency claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds autoregressive score-sequence generation as a possible diversity mechanism and explains that latency benefits depend on available parallelism. It removes the position-only explanation of shuffled LW failures. The existing large-batch limitations and broader limitations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 documents mean input-token counts by method, model and dataset, identifies Thomson Reuters as the proprietary data source, and specifies paragraph-size passages. These are additional disclosures, not established changes to inputs. The code-access link and prompt templates remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 expands citations to pointwise and listwise ranking, including RankVicuna, RankZephyr and FIRST, and discusses entropy/confidence-based ensemble methods. It also clarifies parallel versus sequential test-time scaling. The closest comparisons and central research positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list and conclusion are substantially rewritten around ensemble diversity, test-time scaling and efficiency. Explanations throughout are revised, and a runtime appendix is inserted. This is broader narrative restructuring than isolated language corrections.

P2.justification: V2 adds six three-panel runtime figures and a token-count table, reflows the results pages, and moves table captions below their tables. All eleven original figure images are retained, including prompts relocated from Appendix C to Appendix D.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens practical usefulness by supplementing call-count arguments with runtime distributions, token-use evidence and an explicit parallelism caveat. The original accuracy evidence remains intact. Timing methodology is still sparsely documented, and the shuffled-LW failure discussion is reduced, so the net quality gain is useful but limited.
